subject: Recap: pricing + model mix (follow-up from Thurs call)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@stellarai.com>, Priya Singh <priya@stellarai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: pricing + model mix (follow-up from Thurs call)

Hi Liam / Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and asks so we can size an accurate proposal and target unit economics. I copied Marissa (pricing lead) and Jonas (solutions) so they have context.

Key points from call:
- Primary use: multi-turn customer support assistant + semantic search for knowledge base.
- Expected query pattern: 60% short chats (avg 80 tokens in / out), 30% embeddings-powered retrieval (embedding size 1536, 1 request per user action), 10% reranking for search results (short prompts).
- Peak concurrency: ~120 concurrent users; steady-state daily active users ~6k.
- Target go-live: late Q3.

As we discussed, to scope pricing we need 2 quick confirmations from you:
1) Ballpark monthly token volume (input+output). You mentioned "tens of millions" — can you pick a range? e.g., 10-30M, 30-100M, 100-300M/month.
2) Budget range for inference across hosted vs dedicated options (monthly committed $). Are you aligned to a target $/1M tokens we should optimize toward? You mentioned wanting to keep hosting cost sub-$250 per 1M tokens if possible.

For transparency, I'm attaching the discovery notes and a small pricing model that maps 3 volume tiers to unit costs (hosted vs dedicated). If you confirm volumes and model mix per above (chat/embeddings/rerank), Marissa can put together an initial committed capacity quote and projected monthly spend.

Next steps I propose:
- You reply with the volume range and whether data needs to stay in VPC/on-prem (affects pricing).
- Marissa drafts an initial pricing sheet + recommended model quantization / batching profile.
- Jonas drafts an implementation milestone and estimated engineering effort.

Thanks — short replies totally fine.

Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Attachments: 2026-06-11-stellarai-discovery-notes.pdf (PDF summary), pricing-vs-volume-3-scenarios.xlsx (Excel)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@stellarai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@stellarai.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap: pricing + model mix (follow-up from Thurs call)

Thanks Karthik — that map is helpful. Quick answers from our side: 

1) Volume range: leaning toward the middle tier; expect ~45-70M tokens/month to start, trending up if usage grows after launch. That includes both input and generated tokens.
2) Budget target: we'd like to be in the $150–$220 per 1M tokens range for hosted inference at launch. If a dedicated/reserved model brings it to <$120 per 1M tokens, we can consider a commit.
3) Data locality: must be within our VPC (we require private deployment for PII-handling flows).

On model mix — rough split based on current traffic projections: 
- Chat (multi-turn assistant): 65% of tokens
- Embeddings (semantic search + vector ops): 25% by request volume but only ~10% of token consumption (embeds are small)
- Rerank (short prompts to score results): 10%

We can share a sample of traffic logs if that helps calibrate seq lengths. Priya and I will review the attachments.

Liam
Head of Product, StellarAI
liam@stellarai.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@stellarai.com>, Priya Singh <priya@stellarai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: pricing + model mix (follow-up from Thurs call)

Appreciate the quick clarity, Liam. Useful numbers — we'll run two draft options: a hosted plan hitting ~$180/1M tokens at 50M tokens (mid tier) and a Dedicated commit option that targets ~$95–110/1M tokens depending on commit length and GPU class. A couple of implementation notes that affect both cost and perf: 

- Model choices: for the chat traffic we recommend an opt-quantized 13B chat model (balanced latency/cost). For embeddings we recommend a low-dim production embedding that we can serve on CPU with caching for common queries. For rerank, a small cross-encoder that runs on GPU but is heavily batched.
- Sample model mix we would size for (token consumption basis): chat 70%, embeddings 15%, rerank 15% — this shifts from your request-volume split since embeddings consume fewer tokens but more requests. We'll include both request and token-based splits in the sheets.
- Batching/caching: enabling prefix KV caching for frequent flows can reduce active token count by ~8–12% on our tests; we'll bake conservative numbers into the pricing.

Marissa — can you take Liam/Priya's range (45–70M tokens, VPC requirement) and return a 3-row quote: Hosted (pay-as-you-go), Hosted with 3-month commit, Dedicated (12/24 mo commit) with unit costs and expected latency SLOs? Please include a line that shows projected $/1M tokens after typical batching/caching gains.

Jonas — can you draft a 6-week mile-stone plan for a VPC-onboarding + prompt integration checklist? Liam mentioned late Q3 target, so align milestones to hit an internal P0 by mid-Sept.

Liam — if you can also confirm which regions you want (us-west-2 primary, with eu-west-1 backup?), that'll let us size capacity and costs per region.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a calendar invite for a short pricing review + next steps.

Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks — short confirm from me:
- Volume: agree with 45–70M tokens to start.
- Budget: would prefer to see the hosted $180/1M option and a committed option that gets us under $110/1M; show both 12- and 24-month commit.
- VPC: yes, VPC-only for the production flows that touch user PII; we may pilot non-PII traffic on hosted while we validate.

Please include the HubSpot deal link in the quote email and add our procurement contact (sarah.procure@stellarai.com) once you have numbers. We'll try to give you a definitive capacity commit decision within 2 weeks after the pricing review.
